overview: This Senate resolution names July 25, 2026, as "National Day of the American Cowboy." It praises cowboys and cowgirls for helping settle the American West and describes the values it associates with them, such as honesty, hard work and care for the land. It notes the role of ranching in the economy and the popularity of rodeo. It encourages Americans to mark the day with ceremonies and activities. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 23, 2026.
for: Supporters say the day honors a lasting part of American history and culture and the ranching families who still work the land.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
